research_question: Which event loops repeatedly erase task-relative error while the controller-visible dynamic state returns, producing persistent global loss; can such loops be identified, represented compactly, and broken by preserving a task anchor?
working_method: Search for repeatable event loops with positive task-loss drift. Keep a finite dynamic return state and an explicit additive loss coordinate. Use source-level reset and clipping semantics to determine when increasing loss stops affecting the controller, then fit/check a local return map. Update a loop's recurrence, per-loop loss and feasible repetition count rather than just a single finite scenario label.

theory.specific_candidate_contribution: Characterize a one-sided invariance created jointly by reference resets and observation clipping, despite a fixed external task reference. Use that conditional invariance to lift a closed dynamic loop with positive loss into a family of longer failing event sequences. This is a proposed contribution to investigate, not a verified literature-first claim.
theory.exact_proposition_draft: Let z increase downward and let T_d shift physical height and every internally captured height by d>=0 while preserving velocities, attitude, recurrent state, actuator state and clock phase. Assume (i) plant evolution is vertically translation-equivariant until the task boundary; (ii) capture resets the internal height to the measured current height; (iii) whenever the fixed external reference is active throughout a complete loop, vertical position error is in the same downward saturated branch; (iv) this branch remains valid under downward translation; (v) the complete augmented state after an admissible loop w is exactly T_delta of its start, delta>0, with matching event/clock phase. Then the nth repeated loop ends at T_(n*delta) of the start while the assumptions and input/workspace budget hold. A task-height threshold is crossed by ceil((remaining height budget)/delta) repetitions. Proof is induction using reset equivariance and one-sided clipping invariance. This is conditional; finite traces do not establish assumptions (iii) or (v) for all repeats.
theory.approximate_extension_not_proved: A useful noisy version needs return-state closure/contraction and drift margins, including scheduler branches. P14H's failed long-horizon tube is not evidence that these margins exist. Derive and check a local condition before claiming a reliable repetition horizon.
theory.independent_role: The theory changes the search object to a repeatable loss-producing loop and defines when a measured/predicted loop may update a whole repetition family. The fitted model estimates the return state and drift; ordinary dynamics fitting alone does not establish repeatability or conditional invariance.
missing_conditions_in_draft: For moving trajectories, loop closure must be defined in a frame transported by the external trajectory, and the trajectory itself must repeat under the corresponding transport. Vertical translation alone cannot describe a moving P7 loop.
Absolute timestamps must be advanced consistently; all relative timer ages, scheduler phases and pending message states must return. The reduced CSV cannot establish these conditions.
The pointwise recorded saturation condition is only a candidate regime check. It neither proves recurrence nor positive future drift.

evidence.finding: All 108 captures in 27 P7 sequences reset vertical position error to zero; 27 captures already have more than 0.5m task loss and five exceed 1m. Ten sequences fail height while peak tilt remains below45deg.
T0 D0.38/g0.5 has capture losses -0.003,0.534,0.860,1.200m; late cycle increments0.326 and0.340m. These are suggestive finite-prefix measurements, not a closed-loop certificate.

Ten P11 timeout captures with >0.1m downward task error all increase mean normalized motor command under a one-call intervention restoring the last valid external altitude; mean increase0.08106. This verifies direct controller sensitivity, not flight repair success.

counterevidence: T0 D0.3/g0.5 A45 has nearly complete vertical clipping late, yet capture loss falls from0.592 to0.474m. Saturation and recapture are insufficient to infer positive long-run drift.

Across27 P7 sequences, repeating only the first cycle loss gives0.304m error at the fourth capture. Even repeating the second increment gives0.112m. An unconstrained linear-loss extrapolator is not established as adequate.
P7 exports omit complete attitude/omega, recurrent state, actuators and scheduler caches. Similar exported signals cannot certify complete state recurrence.

Fixed capture repair C already solved all9 evaluated P9 cases. A new repair must justify lower cost, greater repeat robustness or an uncovered mechanism; current command replay does not establish any of these.
No head-to-head superiority over the full-information ordinary grey-box baseline, periodic-template search, or a simple local drift predictor has been established for this candidate.

Prefix-only P7 regime stress test: only 3/27 second cycles have all sampled external vertical errors in the same downward saturated branch. Of those3,2 have positive next-cycle loss; a cheap previous-increment top3 has3/3. Mean next-cycle loss .156m vs .325m. This is a retrospective continuation stress probe with all prefixes already available, not original test-budget evidence or a full cycle-closure-method evaluation.

scope.switching: Potential applies when a closed mode-switch sequence repeatedly recaptures/rebases task anchors and forgets cumulative error. P3/P4 hover switching does not demonstrate such drift, and preserving a persistent absolute anchor may eliminate the condition. No switching advantage claimed.
scope.cross_platform: The structural test depends on reset, clipping and task-anchor semantics; drift magnitude, return-state closure and timing must be identified per platform. No second-platform data exist.
scope.experiment_policy: No new experiments, no SITL, no Thor or SSH. GitHub reads retrieved already archived evidence only.

completion_audit.novel_theoretical_contribution: Not established. Closely related hybrid symmetry abstraction and cycle acceleration already exist; source-conditioned one-sided applicability and a useful approximate result remain open.
completion_audit.potential_beyond_strong_baselines: Not established. Necessary-regime gating alone loses to a cheap prefix drift ordering; no implemented return-state closure algorithm has an independently evaluated advantage.
completion_audit.switching_and_cross_platform_value: structural rationale with explicit conditions only
